definitions.explanation: Having an intense, unwavering attachment to something, often a grudge or goal. Can be neutral (admirably persistent) but more often carries a negative nuance of being obsessively fixated or holding grudges.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{執念深|しゅうねんぶか}い{性格|せいかく}だ。
{執念深|しゅうねんぶか}く{追|お}いかけてくる{相手|あいて}に{恐怖|きょうふ}を{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: I felt fear toward the opponent who pursued me relentlessly.

examples.japanese: あの{刑事|けいじ}は{執念深|しゅうねんぶか}い{捜査|そうさ}で{知|し}られており、{何年|なんねん}も{前|まえ}の{未解決|みかいけつ}{事件|じけん}を{解決|かいけつ}した。
examples.english: That detective is known for his relentless investigations and has solved cold cases from years ago.

notes: Compound adjective formed from {執念|しゅうねん} (tenacity, obsessive determination) + {深|ふか}い (deep). The ～{深|ぶか}い pattern creates adjectives meaning "deeply/intensely ~": {疑|うたが}い{深|ぶか}い (suspicious), {欲|よく}{深|ぶか}い (greedy), {罪|つみ}{深|ぶか}い (sinful). While {執念深|しゅうねんぶか}い can describe admirable persistence (e.g., in investigation or research), it often implies a negative obsessiveness, especially regarding grudges. Related: しつこい (persistent — more colloquial, often negative), {粘|ねば}り{強|づよ}い (persevering — always positive), {根|ね}に{持|も}つ (to hold a grudge).
